# v1.0.6 — the cell behind Table S28

`code/charls_only/97_s28_dominant_2025.R` applies the AWGS 2025 age-specific
cut-offs to the **dominant-hand** reading — the better of two trials in the hand
recorded in `qc002` — instead of the maximum of four trials used in the paper.
This is the combination that Section 4.5 of the manuscript reports as
Supplementary Table S28.

The script rebuilds the dominant-hand value from the trial-level fields
`qc003`–`qc006` (left 1/2, right 1/2), where `qc002` codes the dominant hand as
1 = right, 2 = left, 3 = both equally; a participant with no valid trial in the
recorded dominant hand is left missing rather than defaulting to the other hand.
It returns, by age stratum and for both the 2019 and the 2025 cut-offs,
prevalence of low grip, two-year reversion, the paired difference within the
same participants with a community-cluster bootstrap interval (1,000 resamples),
and the reclassification counts.

## Result

Cohort as in `01_build.R` (`a13 == 0`, `grp19` and `age13` and `male` non-missing):
n = 6,052; 5,987 with a 2011 reading under both rules and 5,886 with a 2013
reading. The 2025 age-specific thresholds and the age strata both use the age at
the **2013 landmark**, matching the note to Table S27.

| Stratum | Cut-off | Low grip, max-of-4 → dominant hand | Difference (95% CI) | Ratio | Reversion, max-of-4 → dominant hand | Difference (95% CI) | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Whole cohort | 2025 | 15.8% → 18.6% | +2.8 (2.3, 3.3) | 1.18 | 60.6% → 57.4% | −3.2 (−4.9, −1.5) | 0.95 |
| 50–64 | 2025 | 13.5% → 16.0% | +2.5 (1.9, 3.1) | 1.19 | 64.4% → 62.2% | −2.3 (−4.8, 0.3) | 0.96 |
| 65 or older | 2025 | 21.6% → 25.2% | +3.6 (2.8, 4.4) | 1.17 | 55.8% → 51.8% | −4.0 (−6.6, −1.6) | 0.93 |
| 50–64 | 2019 | 5.8% → 7.3% | +1.5 (1.2, 2.0) | 1.27 | 73.3% → 71.1% | −2.3 (−6.3, 1.6) | 0.97 |

Because the better of two trials in one hand can never exceed the best of four
trials, the maximum-of-four classification is a subset of the dominant-hand
classification: at the 2025 cut-offs 168 participants in the whole cohort are low
by the dominant-hand rule alone and none the other way round. The reading rule
therefore adds marginal cases; it does not reshuffle the classification.

At ages 50–64 the dominant-hand rule classifies 2.5 percentage points more
participants as low, while the two-year reversion is 2.3 points lower and its
interval reaches zero. The direction of the paper's conclusion is unchanged.

```bash

# reads out/jamda_full.rds and the CHARLS release under _x/

```
